title: Television: John Lennon and Yoko Ono on WABC | 1972
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono took part in a filming session for WABC television on 5 August 1972.

It was part of a campaign by broadcaster Geraldo Rivera, who had recently completed an exposé of the conditions at Willowbrook School in New York City, a state-run institute for children with mental disabilities.

Lennon had seen Geraldo Rivera’s report for ABC TV on the physical and sexual abuse of the children and the poor facilities at the Staten Island school. Rivera decided to launch a fundraising campaign for the children, which became the One To One Festival. It included two headline shows by Lennon at Madison Square Garden on 30 August 1972.

At the start of the month Lennon and Ono were staying in San Francisco, and Rivera flew there to film them as part of the campaign. They were driven around the city, with cameraman Roy Weiss from KGO-TV.

The footage was intended for broadcast on WABC to announce the New York concert. It included Lennon and Ono riding a trolley car, walking in Fisherman’s Wharf and on the Golden Gate Bridge, and discussing the show.

Afterwards, Rivera and Weiss joined Lennon and Ono in the couple’s room at the Stanford Court Hotel, where they sang a selection of rock ‘n’ roll oldies plus their recent single ‘Woman Is The N****r Of The World’.
